conbody.p: Getting rid of a court whose sole focus is on copyright litigation in this day and age does not reflect the needs of our ever-changing digital society. Because violating copyright is so easy to commit, artists whose livelihoods depend on the integrity of their work deserve to have the means to protect it. The current system of litigation through federal court does not make the process of litigating copyright violation claims simple or cheap, turning holders away from investing in the process and draining the pockets of the defendant. Copyright cases congest the federal court system and are relatively petty in the face of other, more heinous cases. With a board whose focus is solely on copyright claims, the process can still be expedited and the cost to file claims can be kept lower, lessening the time one spends requiring legal counsel and therefore lowering the cost overall.
